paragraphs.zh: Tabelle 4:    Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen der allgemeinen Formel (I), worin die Substituenten und Symbole folgende Bedeutungen haben:
paragraphs.en: Table 4:    Compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I), in which the substituents and symbols have the following meanings:
paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. 'Tabelle 4:' is printed in bold and separated from the rest of the caption by a wide tab-like gap, kept here as run-on spaces. The caption runs over two printed lines, breaking after 'worin die'; joined here into one line. The formula reference is a capital I in parentheses. This is the caption of a new table and it fixes the shared substituents for every row of the table lower down the page. A small stray ink mark sits above the 'a' of 'haben' at the end of the second line; it is a scan artifact, not a character or a superscript.

paragraphs.zh: R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH L = CH2 Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.en: R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH L = CH2 Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.notes: The block of substituent definitions printed under the Tabelle 4 caption, laid out in three columns and three rows, centred on the page. It is chemical symbols only with no German prose in it, so zh and en are the same string. Printed with superscripts on the R symbols: R with superscript 4, 5 and 6. L, Y, Z, v and w are printed on the baseline with no superscript, and v and w are lower case as printed. The 2 of every CH2 is printed as a subscript and is transcribed inline. Reading order recorded here is left to right along each printed row, which is how the three columns are aligned on the page. Column alignment is reproduced with run-on spaces and is not significant. The third row has only two entries; the third column of that row is blank on the page.

paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one paragraph per the pass instructions. The cells are compound numbers and substituent symbols, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string; the only German-language token is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), left as printed so the header row matches the source. The header row sits on a grey-shaded band and is printed with superscripts: R with superscript 1, R with superscript 2, R with superscript 3. Subscript digits in OCH2CF3, OCH2CF2CF2H, SO2Me, SO2Et and CF3 are printed as true subscripts and are transcribed inline. This table has only four columns and no 'Physikalische Daten' column. Tabelle 4 begins on this page: the caption, the definition block and the scaffold drawing all appear above the header row, and the numbering opens at 436, continuing the numbering of the earlier tables rather than restarting at 1; recorded as printed and not renumbered. All sixteen rows are on this page, Nr. 436 through Nr. 451, and a ruled bottom border closes the table under Nr. 451. Whether the table continues on the following page cannot be told from this page alone. A small stray dot sits between '445' and the cell rule in the Nr. column of row 445, a faint dot sits in the R3 column of row 446 near the right-hand table border, a faint dot sits in the R2 column of row 448 to the right of SO2Et, and a small dot sits just under the closing border of the table below the R1/R2 column rule; all four read as scan artifacts, not characters. The lower third of the page below the table is blank.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only, centred between the block of substituent definitions and the head of the table
structures.core: Two rings joined by a ketone bridge. LEFT: a six-membered carbocycle drawn as a hexagon with vertical left and right sides, carrying one ring C=C and one exocyclic ring C=O and a ring-bound OH, that is the enol form of a cyclohexane-1,3-dione. RIGHT: a benzene ring drawn as a hexagon with vertical left and right sides and three inner Kekule lines. This is the Tabelle 4 scaffold: the general formula (I) with R4, R5, R6, L, Y, Z, v and w already fixed by the caption block above it, leaving R1, R2 and R3 open for the table rows to supply.
substituents: LEFT RING, top vertex: OH, bond drawn straight up to the label OH
LEFT RING, upper-right vertex: the bridging carbonyl carbon C(=O)Ar, bond drawn up-right; a ring C=C is drawn between this vertex and the OH-bearing top vertex, as an inner parallel line
LEFT RING, lower-right vertex: =O, double bond drawn down-right to a capital O
LEFT RING, bottom vertex: a bare CH2 vertex, no substituent drawn
LEFT RING, lower-left vertex: a bare CH2 vertex, no substituent drawn
LEFT RING, upper-left vertex: a bare CH2 vertex, no substituent drawn
BRIDGE: carbonyl carbon between the two rings, =O drawn straight up to a capital O, single bonds down-left to the left ring's upper-right vertex and down-right to the benzene ipso carbon
BENZENE C1 (upper-left vertex): the bridging C(=O)
BENZENE C2 (top vertex): R2, bond drawn straight up to the label R with superscript 2
BENZENE C3 (upper-right vertex): a plain CH2 vertex drawn up-right, bonded onward down-right to the label R with superscript 1, that is -CH2-R1
BENZENE C4 (lower-right vertex): R3, bond drawn down-right to the label R with superscript 3
BENZENE C5 (bottom vertex): bare, no substituent drawn
BENZENE C6 (lower-left vertex): bare, no substituent drawn
BENZENE Kekule double bonds drawn as inner lines on C1=C6 (left vertical side), C2=C3 and C4=C5

drawings.notes: No arrows and no reagent labels: a single generic scaffold, drawn once above the table so that each numbered row can supply R1, R2 and R3. name and smiles are null because R1, R2 and R3 remain placeholders, so no atom set is determined by the drawing. presented_as is 'intermediate_structure' because the enum offers no value for 'a Markush scaffold heading a table of worked compounds'; it is emphatically NOT prior art, the caption directly above calls these 'Erfindungsgemaesse Verbindungen', compounds according to the invention. Ring positions were read off the drawing geometry only. The benzene numbering used here takes the bridging carbonyl as C1 and runs clockwise; on that numbering the drawn R2 sits at benzene C2, the drawn CH2-R1 at C3 and the drawn R3 at C4. Note the C3 substituent: the linker is drawn out as an explicit unlabelled chain vertex between the ring and the R1 label, not as a letter 'L'; it is read as the single carbon the caption fixes with L = CH2, but the drawing itself carries no L label and no H atoms on that vertex. The left ring is drawn as a plain six-membered ring with no repeat bracket, no R7 substituents and no Y, Z, v or w labels, consistent with the caption fixing Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1 and w = 0. The ring OH is drawn as the two letters O and H, matching R6 = OH in the caption block, so R6 does not appear as a placeholder in the drawing.
